# Ethereum mainnet golden block

`block.pb` is the unchanged `Any.value` payload of a finalized Firehose Stream
response for mainnet block **26,049,575**, captured on **2026-09-25** from
`https://eth.firehose.pinax.network:443`. Its protobuf type is
`sf.ethereum.type.v2.Block`; the source definition is `proto/ethereum.proto`.
The 2,094,485-byte file has SHA-256
`dad74257d32c66a056404add2a5f3360c288faedf0a026e5698394cd9d231b2a`.
`metadata.json` retains only public identity/type information and the payload
checksum. It contains no response cursor, credential or request header.

The payload has 182 transactions (181 succeeded, one reverted), including
legacy, dynamic-fee and blob transactions; 557 receipt logs; 16 withdrawals;
and four system calls. `expected.json` contains the reviewed counts for all
20 mapper tables and 283 selected values on 28 rows. Each selected row names
its original protobuf source path. Integers represented as decimal strings are
computed from the raw big-endian bytes, not from mapper output. Hex expectations
spell out the bytes, including leading zeroes. Nullable values distinguish
absence from zero or empty bytes.

Counts were independently derived by decoding the retained protobuf with Python
protobuf using a descriptor generated by `protoc`. The one reverted transaction
(index 56) has 24 calls and no EIP-7702 authorizations. Its three root-call balance
changes are gas buy, gas refund and transaction fee, and its one root nonce
change persists. Its 12 recorded storage changes are omitted from the 1,526
transaction storage rows. System changes come from block-level changes and
system calls, with no transaction join. The eight zero-row tables are checked
as empty; this block does **not** qualify their nonempty field mappings or every
Ethereum fork. Synthetic unit tests remain useful for those cases.

`blocks/tests/evm_golden.rs` runs entirely offline in `cargo test --workspace`.
It checks standard/extended output, Binary/Hex schemas, and optional fork-step
columns, plus canonical identity on every row. It compares fixed expectations;
it does not calculate its expected values using the mapper under test.

## Refresh or add a fixture

1. Use an explicitly selected provider credential in the environment. The
   capture helper does not load `.env`, and its default selectors are
   `PINAX_API_KEY` / `PINAX_API_TOKEN`; unrelated legacy token variables are not
   consulted. For another endpoint, explicitly select credentials appropriate
   to that destination. Never put a secret value on the command line.
2. Capture one exact finalized block into a **new staging directory**:

   ```sh
   cargo run -p blocks --example refresh_evm_golden --locked -- \
     --block 26049575 --output /tmp/fireparq-evm-golden-candidate
   ```

   The helper requires Ethereum mainnet endpoint metadata, checks payload
   identity/time against response metadata, refuses duplicate/wrong/non-final
   blocks and payloads over 16 MiB, and has a 45-second total deadline. It will
   not overwrite an existing directory and never generates expectations.
3. Inspect the candidate using the original protobuf definition, for example:

   ```sh
   protoc -I proto --decode=sf.ethereum.type.v2.Block proto/ethereum.proto \
     < /tmp/fireparq-evm-golden-candidate/block.pb
   ```

   If your `protoc` does not discover its standard includes, add its installation
   include directory with another `-I`. Review field values, repeated-list counts,
   failed-transaction persistence and source paths independently. Do not bless
   expected output by running the mapper and copying its result. For the same
   block, compare the raw hash/checksum and investigate changes before replacing
   the fixture; public trace representations can change even for a fixed block.
4. Copy the reviewed raw payload and public metadata into a fixture directory,
   update `expected.json` by reference to the raw protobuf, and update this
   provenance/coverage record. `lib_num` is captured response metadata and can
   vary between captures; it is not derived from the block payload. Never retain
   the opaque response cursor, authorization headers or credentials.
5. Run `cargo test -p blocks --test evm_golden --locked`, then the workspace suite.
   Review the binary checksum, expectation changes and any new coverage limits
   in the PR. Add another small block when new fork-specific coverage is needed.
